title: Keep source claims separate until they are genuinely comparable
summary: When sources report apparently conflicting results, compare their measurement definitions, populations and time periods before combining them into one conclusion.

conditions: A brief or decision draws on multiple sources.
Sources report figures or conclusions that appear to point in different directions.
The sources may use different measures, populations, coverage, definitions or comparison periods.
problem_pattern.failure_mode: A synthesis treats unlike measurements as directly contradictory or combines them into one trend, then supplies a causal explanation that none of the sources establishes.

generalised_method.action: For every quantitative claim, retain its source, measure or definition, population or coverage, comparison period, and relevant unit.
Before describing findings as contradictory, check whether the sources measure the same thing over comparable populations and periods.
Where the measures cannot be harmonised, report the findings separately and state exactly why they are not directly comparable.
Separate the observed result from an explanation of why it happened. Do not add a causal account unless the evidence supports it.
Ask an independent reviewer to check that each claim retains its source and qualifiers and that the synthesis has not strengthened the evidence.
Preserve rejected interpretations and the reason for rejecting them in the evidence trail.

applicability: Research briefs and evidence summaries drawing on multiple sources.
Operational reports where metrics, populations or reporting periods differ.
Decision support where apparent disagreement may reflect differing definitions rather than a true conflict.
Any synthesis in which a concise narrative risks overstating what source material establishes.
limitations: The method does not establish whether an individual source is accurate, representative or trustworthy.
Comparability requires domain knowledge of the measures and definitions involved.
Different sources may be comparable on some dimensions and not others; preserve that detail rather than applying a blanket label.
No causal inference method is supplied by this skill.
This candidate has been checked only against the synthetic evidence-reconciliation fixture.

checks: Two synthetic sources reported different directions using different metrics, coverage and comparison periods.
The initial combined causal interpretation was rejected because the supplied evidence did not establish comparability or cause.
The final brief retained each source's metric, coverage and comparison period separately.
An independent verification message checked that the final wording did not add unsupported comparison or causation.
A human made the selection and completion decisions; agent contributions remained separately attributed.
not_established: Accuracy or credibility of real-world source material.
Correct comparability judgements in domains requiring specialist definitions.
Causal explanation of the synthetic measurements.
Universal applicability to every evidence-synthesis task.

reuse_guidance: Use as a candidate practice when synthesising multiple sources. Verify domain-specific measurement definitions and source quality independently; keep non-comparable evidence separate and do not infer causation from direction alone.
